public class Agenda3D extends org.jdesktop.lg3d.wg.Frame3D
A native 3D week-agenda that reads the desktop-wide address book (through ContactDirectory, an adapter over org.jdesktop.lg3d.contacts.ContactStore in lg3d-core) that the production Contacts app edits. The interaction is deliberately one-way: Agenda3D never writes to the contact data, it only invites those contacts to user-created appointments and marks each invitee with a chip beside the block (green = a live contact, grey = an unknown uid).

The window is a plain Frame3D using the standard glassy window decoration (title bar buttons plus the CTRL + right-click flip-to-sticky gesture). Its body is an AgendaGrid week view over a strip of AgendaButton controls. Appointments start empty and are persisted to the user Preferences tree under AppointmentStore.ROOT, so the agenda survives across launches.

Editing model: click a cell to select an existing appointment or to move the creation cursor; New drops a one-hour block at the cursor; the Day/Hr/Dur buttons nudge the selection (or the cursor when nothing is selected); Title cycles a preset caption; Att-/Att+ remove/invite contacts from the shared directory. Every change is saved immediately.

A full-width Send Invites button on the bottom row goes beyond the local attendee list: it composes a real RFC 5545 METHOD:REQUEST invitation (InvitationBuilder) for the displayed week's occurrence of the selection and sends it through the mail app's Jakarta Mail backend (InvitationSender). Like Mail3D, the 3D app installs no password prompt: SAVED-mode accounts send silently, ASK-mode accounts surface the manager's user-safe "no password" error.

A top navigation row (Yr-/Mo-/Wk- and their + counterparts) cycles the displayed week back and forth through the calendar, and Today snaps back to the current week. The grid's title band shows the displayed week's month range and year, so the year is always visible while paging.

When launched with an ISO-8601 yyyy-MM-dd argument - as the 3D calendar widget does when the user double-clicks a day - the grid opens on that day's week instead of the current one (see parseInitialDate(java.lang.String[])). Launched with no argument (the start menu), it opens on today as before.
